validity.researcher_notes: This is a genuinely unstable, multi-era, direction-dependent spec, not a case of finding nothing. Chronology as best reconstructed: (1) Nov 1, 2000 original FERC application (Docket CP01-22/23-000; Federal Register 2000-11-15, FR Doc 00-29206) proposed the pipeline to 'carry 500,000 Mcf per day' (=500 MMcf/d), flow direction Arizona-to-Mexico only, at commissioning. Corroborated independently by Oil & Gas Journal, Dec 26, 2000 ('500 MMcfd capacity... companies have signed agreements for more than half'). (2) In 2007 a bidirectional-flow expansion was approved (per Wikipedia's citation to a 2007 Reuters article I could not independently re-fetch -- Reuters returned HTTP 401 to direct access and the Wayback Machine API rate-limited (429) on two attempts; not re-verified as an independent primary source in this pass) enabling US-bound imports. (3) Pre-XPress (~2018-2022), naturalgasintel reported directional capacities of approximately 500 MMcf/d southbound and 614-695 MMcf/d northbound (not independently re-verified against raw source text -- WebFetch summary only, apparent paywall/JS on direct fetch). (4) The North Baja XPress project (P2569; FERC Docket CP20-27-000, approved 2022, Reuters May 30 2023) added approximately 495,000 dekatherms/day (~495 MMcf/d) of INCREMENTAL firm delivery capacity toward the Mexico border -- confirmed directly in the FERC EA itself ('The Project would provide transportation of feed gas for Sempra LNG and IEnova's Energia Costa Azul liquified natural gas (LNG) terminal... approximately 495,000 dekatherms per day (495 million cubic feet per day) of incremental firm delivery capacity'), and again by EIA's Today in Energy (eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=52478): the XPress project 'modifies existing facilities and compressor stations along its 86-mile North Baja Pipeline' adding 0.5 Bcf/d for LNG-terminal feed-gas export. (5) Current TC Energy operator-page figures (tcplus.com/North%20Baja, fetched 2026-09; not independently cross-checked against a second operator page in this pass) state 'Southbound: 972 MMcf/d; Northbound: 576.5 MMcf/d' -- roughly consistent with 500 (original) + ~495 (XPress increment) approx 995-1000 for the southbound/export direction post-expansion, which is an internally coherent story across sources (2) that no single source states a flat, undated 600 MMcf/d figure that matches the sheet. Recommend: leave Capacity's fills entry UNRESOLVED (below) and route to an update pass that pulls North Baja's actual FERC Statement of Rates / Index of Customers tariff filing, which would give the dated, authoritative, single-direction design-capacity figure GEM's schema calls for.

summary: P0226 (North Baja Gas Pipeline, Main, Ehrenberg AZ-to-Ogilby CA) is a real, well-documented, FERC-certificated interstate pipeline in service since 2002; existence, classification, and non-duplicate status against sibling row P2569 (North Baja XPress, a compression-only expansion of the same system, no new pipe) are all confirmed with high-tier, independently-corroborated sourcing. All 14 worklist units were researched: Status, Fuel, Proposal (2000-11), StartYear1 (2002), Length (129 km), Diameter (30/36 in), Location (Ehrenberg AZ to Ogilby CA), Operator, and Owner (North Baja Pipeline LLC, 100%) were all confirmed and filled/REFS_ADDED at high tier off primary FERC/Federal Register documents (2000, 2002, 2020) plus independent trade press (Oil & Gas Journal, EIA) and operator pages (TC Energy). Construction (2002) was filled at medium tier via a BLM right-of-way-grant date rather than an explicit 'construction began' statement. Capacity, Pressure, FuelSource, and SegmentCost remain UNRESOLVED: Capacity is the most significant open item -- the sheet's flat 600.00 MMcf/d does not cleanly match any single dated primary source (found figures range from the original 500 MMcf/d one-directional 2000 design capacity to asymmetric 972/576.5 MMcf/d post-2022-XPress-expansion figures), so it is flagged as a spec-caveat validity concern (contested, not endorsed) rather than force-matched or falsely marked as nothing-found; an update pass should pull North Baja's actual FERC tariff filing to pin this down. Pressure, FuelSource, and SegmentCost had no adequate primary sourcing found (SegmentCost's only available figure is an aggregate binational $230M project total spanning a separate Mexican pipeline GEM does not track here) and are documented as UNRESOLVED with notes on what was searched.
